description.narrative:
Over the last three years CAFOD with funds from DFID and CI members has implemented a SFP feeding projects at estimated 4 million GBP in response to high levels of acute and chronic malnutrition attributed to food insecurity. The projects were implemented through three Eparchies of Karen, Asmara and Barentu, benefiting over 30,000 children and mothers.
Although SFP has contributed effectively to improved nutrition status among the beneficiaries, it has not been sustainable, as most children deteriorated back the original health status once discharged from the project. The recovery rates have been extremely low pointing to poor food support systems at the house hold level. As part of project implementation, the Eparchy of Karen collected and collated information on viable food security projects that will facilitate households to produce and access adequate food to sustain good maternal and child nutrition.
The purpose of the project is to enhance house hold food security at the grass root level and improve the livelihood of the targeted areas The project will strive to ensure 1. Households vulnerable to malnutrition are planting crops and using sustainable cooking methods to improve the quality and diversity of their diet. 2. Vulnerable communities have access to increased livelihood opportunities and training. By protecting women rights protect women's rights to economic opportunities by enhancing their economic capacity at household level
3. Targeted communities have Iincreased access to safe and potable water sources
